questionText:
Let $p$ and $q$ be the following propositions:

$p$: Fail grade can be given.

$q$: Student scores more than 50% marks.

Consider the statement: “*Fail grade cannot be given when student scores more than 50% marks.*”

Which one of the following is the CORRECT representation of the above statement in propositional logic?
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

Given the propositions:
• $p$: Fail grade can be given.
• $q$: Student scores more than 50% marks.

The given statement is: "Fail grade cannot be given when student scores more than 50% marks."

A statement of the structure "$A$ when $B$" translates to the conditional proposition "If $B$, then $A$" ($B \rightarrow A$).

Here:
• Condition $B$ = "student scores more than 50% marks", which corresponds to $q$.
• Result $A$ = "Fail grade cannot be given", which is the negation of $p$, i.e., $\neg p$.

Substituting these into $B \rightarrow A$ yields:
$q \rightarrow \neg p$

Therefore, the correct option is (A).
